title: The Designer's CLO Journey: Crafting a Qixi Festival-Themed Beaded Embroidery Dress with CLO under the Autumn Moon
transcript:
Hello everyone, today we are going to learn how to make a new style of handmade embroidered pearl dress.  
Since today is our Qixi Festival, I wish you all a happy Qixi Festival.  
Qixi Festival had a special meaning in ancient times—it was a day to pray for the best.  
Today, we will make this handmade embroidered pearl dress together in CLO3D.  
This is a detail of our embroidery.  
This style will also be used in our new 2026.1 feature: the new method of handmade embroidery and the four-line function.  

Now, open CLO3D, click on the canvas window, and import the materials for everyone.  
This material can be obtained by replying “free material” on the official account.  
Insert the Qixi style ZPRJ project file.  
For this style, we have already prepared a semi-finished product for everyone in advance.  
It uses the virtual model 3D pen function.  
And it has already been displayed as a template beforehand.  
If you want to learn more about this tool, you can refer to the Financial Theme of the National Day issue.  

Next, let’s work on this template.  
The template is processed to have a symmetrical effect.  
These two front templates, right-click and open edit.  
For the other two templates, including the back, just press Ctrl+D to duplicate and hold down to align.  
Then, let’s check the sewing lines.  
Sew the two sewing lines at the back.  
Simulate it.  
Okay.  

Next, let’s import the skirt.  
Click on Connect.  
This skirt can be used directly.  
We provide this material on Connect.  
You can search for it directly in Connect.  
This is the name of the skirt.  
Add it to the shopping cart.  
After placing the order, you can use it directly in Cloud.  
Since I have already purchased it, I will drag it in directly.  
Click to add.  
Select clothing.  
Click confirm.  
Okay.  
The skirt has now been imported.  
Let’s activate and hide the top shirt.  
This skirt will be slightly larger than our model.  
Let’s first place it at the model’s waist.  
Then simulate it.  
Select all skirt panels.  
Reduce its scale to 95%.  
Okay.  
Simulate again.  
Let it show the effect of a slightly tight skirt.  
This skirt is the base of our dress.  
We will add some decorative panels to this skirt to present a rich decorative effect.  

Next, let’s adjust the skirt length.  
First, use the edit curve tool.  
Delete a few curve points here.  
Then use the edit curve tool again.  
Hold Shift and select these two panel lines.  
Shift them by 110 mm respectively.  
Perform the same operation for the front and back.  
The overall skirt length is shortened by 110 mm, which is 11 cm.  
Then raise its front and middle points to create a curved effect.  
Adjust the panel lines to make them smoother on both sides.  
Okay.  
Simulate and pull the skirt.  
Now the skirt is tight, so we need to be careful when pulling it.  
Okay.  

Next, let’s adjust the waist part.  
Make the waist wider.  
Select these two lines.  
Increase by 25 mm.  
Do the same for the back waist.  
Increase by 25 mm.  
When raising, after pressing the left key, right-click, and you can enter the movement distance.  
We can look at the translucent surface.  
Its current length is basically just right.  
Click here to adjust it.  
Then we can pull the skirt.  
It’s tight.  
Anticipate the movement.  
Then pull the waist part.  
Please look here.  
Okay, now let’s make the waist thinner.  
This is the waist. Let’s adjust it.  
Look at the center of the skirt.  
Can you see this?  
This is the center straight line.  
I will simulate it and let it be worn outside the skirt.  
Check left and right to see if the garment is flat.  
Then select a panel and freeze it.  

Next, use the 3D pen clothing tool to draw a line on the skirt panel.  
The curve should be like this: left-click to start, press Ctrl to draw a curve, double-click to finish.  
Then draw the second line the same way.  
Left-click to start, press Ctrl to draw a curve, slowly go down.  
Then draw the third line, double-click to finish.  
Next, draw the fourth line, double-click to finish.  

Next, use the 3D pen tool to adjust the curves.  
Press Ctrl to start.  
Here is the curve we just drew.  
Next, draw the third line.  
Now we see the curve of the skirt panel.  
What should we do with it?  
Check it.  
The skirt curve is rounder than the skirt panel line.  
The gap between several lines is relatively deep.  
This will make the skirt panel more layered.  
After the adjustment is almost done, press Shift to select all lines and select the internal shape.  
After selecting the internal shape, select these lines.  
First, lock all outer outlines, then select the frame, copy these internal lines, and paste them on the back.  
Then slightly adjust the start and end points to naturally connect to the back angle.  
Then select these points, right-click, and align them to the outline.  
When adjusting the internal line with sound, we can flip it to check—it will be more intuitive.  
Here we can optimize the triangle outline to reduce some drawdowns and make the curves smoother.  
The same applies here; right-click to choose optimal drawdown, left-click to select optimal drawdown.  
After mostly finishing the adjustment, delete all the 3D pencil lines.  

Next, let’s make these panels.  
There are 4 layers in total: 5 layers in the front and 4 layers in the back.  
Let’s start with the 4th layer, then the last layer is copied directly.  
Use the round panel tool.  
We work from the bottom up, making the largest panel first.  
For this diameter, enter 910 mm.  
Click OK.  
This is a zipper panel; move it to one side.  
Let’s make the bottom layer first.  

Next, use the round panel tool again for the bottom layer.  
In the middle, left-click.  
Enter diameter 480 mm, click OK.  
Then turn it into a hole.  
Make inner lines on both sides of the front and back, then cut it off.  
Take a semicircle.  
Based on this panel, adjust its group.  
Select the two middle lines, move them down to the front section.  
Make a back-long shape.  
Adjust the width of the back to make it diagonal.  
Delete this inner line.  
Pull it out to adjust to an oblique T-shape.  
Then choose to align, open, adjust position.  
Cool down our skirt panel.  

Then sew the skirt panels together.  
Sew the short side first, i.e., the skirt side, then sew the long side, i.e., the skirt panel.  
Wait for sewing to finish.  
Okay.  
After sewing, simulate it.  
The bottom skirt panel is done.  

Next, copy this version.  
Paste it.  
Use the positioning tool to drag it down to the corresponding position and pull it out a little bit.  
Then sew this skirt to the third layer skirt.  
We can adjust this skirt to be a little shorter for a more layered effect.  
Then continue to copy and paste to make the second layer of the skirt.  

Thank you for watching.  
First, freeze the third layer skirt and drag the second layer skirt down.  
It will be less likely to pass through.  
This fabric piece needs M by N free sewing.  
Sew the M-line first, press return to complete.  
Then select the N-line, press return to complete.  
Thank you for watching.  
Simulate, arrange the board.  

Next, make the top layer of the board.  
Draw a circle again.  
Diameter 580.  
Inner circle, left-click.  
Diameter 295, click OK.  
Change to a hole.  
Same operation as before.  
Drag the circle down.  
Draw front and back inner lines and cut off.  
Adjust angles and lines so that when opened, the lines will not clash and there is a small gap in the middle.  

Next, sew this board.  
Move it up near the skirt.  
Freeze it.  
Simulate the next board layer.  
The amount of this board will be a bit more because we are using a round board, so the total quantity will be richer.  
You can use hardening to help pull.  
I also used a fixed needle here to help pull the board and organize its shape.  
After arranging, unfreeze and simulate.  

Next, adjust its arc.  
Use drag to adjust the size and shape of the round pot.  
You can also adjust the length of the round pot to make its edge smoother.  
Repeat the process for the other four pieces.  
Make the back piece.  
Drag the positioning tool to the back of the model.  
Adjust position and freeze the front pieces.  
Then sew these round pots simultaneously.  
First sew the skirt, then the white part of the skirt, then the top part.  
The upper part is also sewn with M-N free sewing.  
Pin the M-line and press return.  
Sew the N-line and press return to complete stitching.  
Finally, sew the first panel of the skirt using M-N free sewing.  
Remember to switch to fold-sew.  
Simulate, pull to adjust the skirt shape, avoid penetration.  
Activate the skirt and simulate again.  
Sort out the skirt shape.  
Change the color to dark for better viewing.  
Adjust the height of the second layer skirt.  
You can adjust skirt layers according to your aesthetic and ideas.  

Thank you for watching.  
See you next time.  
The skirt is almost done.  
Next, let’s adjust the top and add details.  
Freeze the skirt.  

Now, make a white decorative line on the top, similar to middle-aged clothing.  
It’s a method of wrapping the edge.  
Choose an inner border at the edge.  
Set an inner border of 5 mm.  
Do the same for the two side panel lines.  
After making the inner border, choose this panel.  
Find the outer colon layer, fill it, and make a colon layer.  
Then choose to cut and delete the panel inside.  
Fill the sewing line.  
Simulate.  
You can see this is a relatively floating effect.  
There are three of them.  
This is a common method.  
Two panels.  
Repeat the same operation for the other panel.  
Choose the outer colon layer, cut it off, delete unnecessary parts, fill the sewing line.  
Sew with a thread only.  

Then pull these two panels, Ctrl+D to copy and paste to the other side.  
Simulate.  
Do the same for the back.  
Add a 5 mm inner line.  
Go to the outer colon layer, cut, delete unnecessary parts, fill sewing line.  
This method wraps the edge and strip, making it more floating and stable.  
After lining up the other half of the back, the detail is almost done.  

To make it more stable, we can reduce the diameter of the example a bit smaller.  
I changed it to 8 mm.  
After everything is disassembled, simulate again.  
Open random color.  

Next, replace the fabrics for the clothes.  
The upper and lower body fabrics are pink body flower prints.  
This fabric piece is used.  
In the canvas window, the pink body flower fabric is in the material.  
Drag it directly in.  
First, apply this fabric to all clothing panels.  
The upper body uses fabric 1, a pure mesh transparent fabric.  

Next, copy another fabric for the lower skirt.  
Select all skirts and apply the second fabric.  
Change the color to pink, click apply and close.  
Change the color of the second fabric.  
Now you can see the skirt color is 2 to 3 colors.  
Reduce the opacity of the upper half fabric to 2 because it is in a pure shadow state.  
Pinch this fabric to have a lifting function because it needs to be attached tightly under the chest.  
The chest fabric can also be pinched.  
Simulate.  
It needs a more three-dimensional, full shape.  
Pinch the side of the bag.  
This fabric has a small hole due to its small size.  
Use the setting layer tool to apply this bag to its layer separately.  
Click the left button to set the top sheet, then the left button for the bottom sheet.  
Done once.  
Layer setting.  
Simulate.  
These sheets go to their places without penetration.  

Next, make the hand embroidery part.  
There is an embroidery sticker prepared in the material.  
Take the sticker out and drag it to the door of the room.  
Make a curved sheet 300 mm x 300 mm, click OK.  
Turn off this sticky show to avoid affecting viewing.  
Generally, embroidery flowers cover the clothes and cross sewing lines, so we need to make a separate sheet for it to attach to the clothes.  
I made a single sheet here.  
Freeze unnecessary sheets and deactivate them for faster simulation.  
Drag this sheet to the model’s chest.  
Put this embroidery sticker on the sheet.  
Use fabric 1, the semi-transparent sticker.  
Rotate the embroidery flower piece.  
Adjust the position with the positioning tool.  
Place it on the edge of the chest, partially embroidered on the chest and partially on the gauze on the chest.  
Set the pressure on this plate to -10 (negative pressure), then harden it.  
Open simulation under pressure to let it be absorbed by the model.  
Freeze the top plate for easier adjustment.  
Change pressure to -7 (highest pressure) for close absorption.  
Adjust pressure between -7 and -2 to vary absorption.  
Cancel hardening and simulate.  
Pull to adjust to desired position and state.  
Try to let the flower cover its edge line for a natural costume look.  
Adjust strength to 10 to make the board more floating.  
Rotate the flower to fit the model’s shape.  

Next, look at the flower shape and draw the inner line.  
No need to draw very close to the edge because beads will be added later.  
The beads are made with copper wire.  
If copper wire is too close to the edge, the OBJ copper wire will break.  
Draw a rough outline.  
After positioning, cut it off and delete unnecessary boards.  
Simulate again.  
Use a fixed needle to assist and slightly adjust position.  

Next, fix its position with the eye-catching tool.  
On the flower, left-click to add eye-catching points along its edge.  
Add a few points in the middle for accuracy.  
Select all eye-catching points with the move button.  
Right-click, set layer to 2.  
Now the flower is fixed on the outfit.  
Change eye-catching point opacity to 0.  
Delete fixed needles.  
Simulate.  
The flower is fixed due to eye-catching points.  
Adjust pressure to -1.  

Next, how to make a bead.  
As mentioned earlier, our bead is made with thread and small beads in rows.  
The flower thread is made with a button, which is made with thread.  
We need to draw corresponding inner thread lines on the flower.  
Now I add some thread lines, pressing Ctrl to sketch curves.  
Double-click to finish.  
Create inner lines with curves, adjust curves.  
Select inner line border and set border to 2.5.  
Hook on both sides.  
Extend count to 4 or 3 because beam width is about 3.  
After adding inner lines, adjust details.  
Select ends, adjust inner lines similarly.  

Next, drag all beam materials for everyone: beam slices, round beads, interval beads, tube beads.  
Use these beams next.  
Make another inner line, use line section line tool to add beam slices.  
Select the curve and copy a group of beam layers in the middle.  
Change to a light color to create petal layers with darker and lighter petals.  
Copy another one.  
For the next two sets, use a lighter color, a light yellow.  
Click and close.  
Select the curve again to smooth corners.  
Use round beads and copy one.  
Use free line, set to white, hook a circle like a small pearl.  
Hook and select the curve.  
This is a flower pattern made with beam slices.  
Repeat the same for the other flower edge.  
Draw inner lines, add small round beads and lines.  
For different colors or bead effects, feel free to be creative.  

After hooking, use the round bead line and line section line to add once.  
Hook the flower pattern’s inner line edges.  
Use editor line tool to hook the curve for smoother corners.  

After hooking, choose the flower pattern to make lighting effects.  
Same method as before: draw many inner lines.  
Because the flower pattern border interferes more with inner lines, sometimes add points at intersections and divide them.  
Delete unnecessary points and adjust lines accordingly.  
Add light color changes to draw light effects.  
Adjust width or thickness of inner lines as needed.  

Now it is a small bead effect visible at about 10% opacity.  
Since oatmeal itself is golden, I used a golden tube here.  
Add it directly using line segment line.  
To adjust tube diameter, change parameter to 0.5 for thinner tube.  
Adjust length for roundness; I set it to 1.5.  
Add other oatmeal and inner lines.  
Make small pearl effect.  
Select opposite direction, diameter 1, confirm.  
Use round tube and line segment line.  
Change diameter to 1 and confirm.  
Modify color and inner color.  
Draw two inner lines with diameter 3 mm.  
X-ray line segment length and confirm.  
Select these lines, right-click, delete excess lines.  
Add corresponding lines: one light gold, one white.  

Next, make flower petals with a button plus a small pearl.  
Add button material to the window.  
Left-click to add button.  
Adjust button position.  
Alt-click select and delete unnecessary parts.  
Adjust length and width to be bigger; set both to 2.  
Adjust material to metal.  
Make two more small lines similarly to show pearl shine effect.  
This process makes a handmade pearl wall showing a shining effect.  

Next, make a pearl leaf with gradient.  
Draw a line in the middle as with petals.  
Add inner lines on both sides.  
Add gradient of 2.  
Delete excess inner lines.  
Adjust inner lines’ positions to follow leaf shape.  
Select lines, right-click, add gradient.  
Divide inner points and delete excess lines.  
Drag and organize lines to fit leaf shape.  
After arranging, add a bead to the leaf.  
Adjust to a gold color similar to the base.  
Choose silk or metal bead color.  
See which looks better.  
Copy and make a gradient color.  
Adjust color to light green, apply, close.  
Adjust material if needed.  
Copy a new line, change color to darker green, use again.  
Manually adjust diameter for wider gradient.  
Copy inner line and paste onto inner line.  
Adjust according to the leaf shape.  
Adjust petal inner line color based on overall color for final adjustment.  
Make pearl thread bead size smaller.  
Make another inner thread of flower thread.  
Add this thread to enrich flower layers.  
Open layers.  

Next, make lower half skirt details.  
Use new stitch method of our paper editor and tear function.  
See the tear effect.  
Open CLO3D.  
First untwist the upper body; after finishing, turn it over.  
Turn on front piece; back piece same operation.  
Simulate.  
Select the plate and do furrowing.  
Use sewing thread tearing and edge tearing tools.  
Sewing thread tearing requires rum stripping for tear effect.  
Select plate line and add 5 mm internal groove compassion.  
Change internal line.  
Select internal line and adjust middle point.  
Combine overlapping points.  
Select two internal lines, right-click, cut seam.  
Drag cut board out.  
Use sewing line tearing tool.  
Select sewing line to tear, left-click start, right-click end.  
Alternatively, use editor sewing line tool, right-click, add sewing line tearing.  
Add tearing to whole sewing line.  
Select sewing line; finished line shows green.  
In the attribute editor, you can edit data.  

Freeze other boards and the board to be pulled out.  
See pulling effect—like tearing edge.  
Freeze other boards.  
As sewing line breaks, it forms a natural torn edge.  
The key is you don’t need to create shape yourself; physical simulation creates torn results.  
After pulling all edges off, place on the ground and right-click to save.  
This keeps the torn edge effect.  

Next, use editor tearing function.  
Select sewing lines, activate, all edge effects disappear.  
Select material to use same material and color as fabric.  
Select main outline line, turn off end-to-end activation to hide main outline.  
There is also a long line—turn off end-to-end.  
Hair-cutting line can be adjusted here—density, thickness, length, etc.  
Parameters are close to our hair.  
Coverage is generally 100%.  
Length can be up to 20 mm with adjustable difference in length and track.  
Adjust parameters as needed.  
Adjust direction too.  
This makes hair-cutting effect of tearing more natural.  
After adjusting, save parameters.  
Save to known location and keep file secret.  
Click save.  
Later, parameters can be reused without adjustment.  

Next, use same method on upper board to add hair-cutting effect.  
Review previous operations on this board.  
Before hair-cutting effect, copy a plate on the front.  
Add another layer to make lace-effect plate to enrich skirt layers.  
Copied plate here, so fill sewing line again.  
Click fold.  
In fabric, find lace fabric.  
Drag directly to this plate.  
Simulate.  
After simulating, check final effect.  
Adjust length again, showing a bit below plate edge.  

Next, go to internal line.  
Right-click, select internal line diameter 5 mm, expand to 1, confirm.  
Check points for alignment.  
Right-click, select cut seam, drag plate out and put aside.  
Repeat for two sewing lines.  
Simulate.  
Manually tear apart to show fur edge effect.  
This board has more layers and some plates hidden.  
Turn on some interference plates to pull out edge plates easily.  
Hide some interference plates after pulling out edges.  
After all are pulled out, store the edge plates.  

Select all plates, display all, activate all skirt plates.  
Use editor to tear them apart.  
Open saved skirt parameters.  
Perform same operation on other side.  
Open saved parameters.  
Skirt effect applied.  

Next, make hollow laser display with new editor.  
This is the hollow laser effect.  
Select all plates, activate, hide color.  
Simulate.  
Select honey-colored flower neck fabric.  
Copy fabric.  
Apply these two fabrics to plates needing needle effect.  
Change material type to wool product.  
Now it shows wool product effect.  
Default is belt needle; change needle method to flat needle.  

Open paper editor.  
Our new paper editor has preview window at top and panel at bottom.  
Click arrow icon on panel’s right to close panel and see preview more clearly.  
Set number of paper pieces.  
In simulation, control physical properties of paper.  
Click top screen to display paper in front of simulation.  
Open preview window to edit.  
When preview window is active, simulation clicks are disabled.  
To simulate again, turn off preview window.  

Next, look at new needle methods.  
Modify horizontal line number to 10, line thickness to 0.5, circle density to 11.  
Click apply.  
Try to see update in 3D window.  

Look at three new needle methods: circle, circle and corner.  
First, circle method.  
Select circle tool.  
Click on a needle; it hangs on top row and forms circle structure.  
Click a few more times to make circle structure more obvious.  
Click apply.  
3D window shows three-dimensional expansion effect.  

Adjust piece data: line thickness 1, density 6.  
Apply.  
Click circle tool; selected needles highlight yellow.  
Click selected area again and press circle to move left or right.  
By default, row adjusts to desired location.  
Depending on effect, bloom these lines on selection.  
Set different hole effects.  
Click model, then application.  
Hole line appears on costume.  

Look at flower pattern settings.  
After clicking flower, a pop-up window appears.  
Set number of needles on upper and lower layers separately and width of joint part.  
Choose twist direction: left or right.  
Set upper and lower layer needles for positive or negative needles.  
After setting, left-click to see twist.  
Click simulation; flower appears.  
Click application.  
3D window shows twist.  

Next, use circle and other needles to show hollow lace effect.  
Change thread thickness to 2, loop density to 3.  
Apply.  
Use circle needle method, left-click to move a larger loop once to create hollow effect.  
Move smaller loop on side, switch left and right.  
Other side same operation.  
Create different hollow effects by design.  
Use reverse needle on both sides for diversified needle methods.  
Add floating threads.  
Turn on simulation, click apply.  
Hollow lace needle effect appears.  
Enlarge flat data for more even effect.  
Simulate and apply again.  

Our style is basically complete.  
Look overall.  
On back side, use needle plate, select two corresponding needle plates, click apply.  
Many other updates and detailed explanations for piece converter and four functions will be updated later.  
Pay attention to new function explanations for detailed introductions.  

Finally, change posture.  
This posture is included in free material.  
When changing posture, you see arms behind.  
Changing posture may cause clothes penetration.  
Right-click, select reverse-activated virtual model.  
After reverse activation, change posture again.  
Since arm is reverse-activated without physical calculation, it won’t penetrate clothes.  
After changing, activate arm again.  
If arm is reverse-activated, arms are reverse-activated.  
Change posture.  
Switch off model.  
Shift fur position left and right as needed.  
To change posture, press left button and hold reverse-activated button.  
Model moves to center; top part moves center.  
If model is reverse-activated, press this button to center and adjust outfit quality.  
Simulate.  
After simulation stabilizes, turn off simulation and open Connect.  
Add settings to model here.  
I used earrings and shoes here.  
Search keywords and buy in mall; all are free.  

Finally, go into simulation window to check overall effect.  
Simulate first.  
Skirt appears a little black because hair product display is off.  
Turn on hair product display and simulate again.  
Check effect.  
Zoom in to check embroidery and beads.  
From close, some penetration is visible due to embroidery sticker having 2 mm simulation degree.  
Use edit thread function to frame all threads.  
Change Z-axis distance to 2.  
Return to simulation and check effect.  
All threads now float.  
Buttons are the same.  
Frame all buttons.  
Change thread length to 2; buttons lift.  
Simulate again.  
Button parts appear on embroidery pattern.  
Zoom in to check.  
Some penetrations and compression deformation occur due to inner thread compressed against grid.  
Choose this sticker version, harden it, or paste a layer.  
Flatten compressed inner thread.  
Inner thread becomes flat, OBJ thread shows original state with no large compression.  
Simulate synchronization again.  
Now inner thread shows normal effect.  

Above is the tutorial for making this new embroidered pearl dress.

chunks.title: The Designer's CLO Journey: Crafting a Qixi Festival-Themed Beaded Embroidery Dress with CLO under the Autumn Moon
chunks.content: # The Designer's CLO Journey: Crafting a Qixi Festival-Themed Beaded Embroidery Dress with CLO under the Autumn Moon This document details the step-by-step process of creating a handmade embroidered pearl dress inspired by the Qixi Festival using CLO3D software. It covers garment construction, fabric manipulation, embroidery techniques, beadwork, and advanced CLO3D functions including new features like handmade embroidery, the four-line function, and paper editor effects. --- ## Introduction to the Qixi Festival-Themed Dress and CLO3D Setup This section introduces the cultural significance of the Qixi Festival and the garment style—a handmade embroidered pearl dress designed in CLO3D. It highlights new 2026.1 CLO3D features: a novel handmade embroidery method and the four-line function. - Qixi Festival: An ancient Chinese festival for praying for the best. - Dress: Handmade beaded embroidery dress with intricate pearl details. - Software: CLO3D 2026.1 with new embroidery and four-line features. - Materials: Available via CLO's official account by requesting “free material.” - Project file: Qixi style ZPRJ project used as a template. - Virtual model 3D pen function utilized in the design. --- ## Importing and Preparing Base Garments in CLO3D This section explains importing base garments, setting up templates, and initial adjustments for the dress in CLO3D. - Import the Qixi style ZPRJ project and pre-prepared semi-finished product. - Use virtual model 3D pen for template visualization. - Duplicate front and back templates symmetrically (Ctrl+D) and align. - Check and sew back sewing lines, then simulate. - Import the skirt from CLO Connect, purchase or drag directly if owned. - Adjust skirt size: place at model’s waist, scale skirt panels to 95% for a tighter fit. - Adjust skirt length by editing curve points and shifting lines by 110 mm (11 cm). - Create curved skirt effect by raising front and middle points; smooth panel lines. - Adjust waist width by increasing lines by 25 mm on front and back. - Use translucent surface mode and movement distance input for precise adjustments. - Simulate and refine fit, ensuring garment flatness and symmetry. - Freeze panels selectively to maintain shape during adjustments. --- ## Creating Decorative Skirt Panels and Layering This section covers designing multi-layered skirt panels with round shapes, sewing, and layering techniques. - Use the round panel tool to create skirt layers from bottom up: - Largest panel diameter: 910 mm (zipper panel, moved aside). - Bottom layer panel diameter: 480 mm, converted to a hole. - Draw inner lines on front and back, cut to create semicircle shape. - Adjust groupings and positions for diagonal and oblique T-shaped back. - Sew panels starting from short sides (skirt edges), then long sides. - Simulate after sewing each layer. - Copy and paste panels to create multiple layers (up to five layers in front, four in back). - Adjust layer lengths for a rich decorative effect. - Use M-N free sewing to attach layers: - Sew M-line, press return. - Sew N-line, press return. - Freeze layers appropriately during assembly to prevent penetration.

Adjust layer lengths for a rich decorative effect. - Use M-N free sewing to attach layers: - Sew M-line, press return. - Sew N-line, press return. - Freeze layers appropriately during assembly to prevent penetration. --- ## Adjusting the Skirt Shape and Edge Details This section details modifying skirt arcs, sewing edges, and creating layered effects with hardening and pinning. - Adjust round panels using drag tools to refine the arc and smooth edges. - Use hardening and fixed needle functions to shape and stabilize skirt edges. - Sew round pots (decorative pieces) simultaneously with skirt layers. - Change skirt layers’ height and color for visual clarity and layering aesthetics. --- ## Adding Decorative Top Details and Edge Wrapping This section explains creating white decorative lines on the top garment panels using inner borders and colon layers for edge wrapping. - Create 5 mm inner borders on edges and side panel lines. - Generate outer colon layers, fill, cut, and delete inner parts for floating edge effect. - Fill sewing lines with thread only to stabilize edges. - Mirror panels with Ctrl+D for symmetrical decoration on back and front. - Adjust inner border width down to 8 mm for better stability. - Simulate with color adjustments to verify effect. --- ## Applying Fabrics and Layering for Realistic Textures This section covers fabric application, opacity changes, and layering for realistic material effects. - Use pink body flower print fabric for upper and lower body. - Upper body fabric: pure mesh transparent fabric (fabric 1). - Lower skirt fabric: second fabric with pink tones, 2-3 color variations. - Reduce upper fabric opacity to 2 for shadow effect. - Use pinching tool to create lifting and tight attachment around chest and bag areas. - Fix small holes in fabric with setting layer tool: - Assign top and bottom sheets to fabric layers. - Simulate to confirm no penetration. --- ## Designing and Positioning Embroidery Stickers This section explains how to add hand embroidery using embroidery stickers, curved sheets, and pressure settings for natural fit. - Create a curved sheet (300 mm x 300 mm) to attach embroidery sticker. - Use semi-transparent fabric 1 for embroidery sticker. - Position sticker over chest edge, partially covering fabric and gauze. - Set pressure on sheet from -10 to -7 for absorption and hardening. - Freeze the top plate for easier adjustment. - Adjust pressure between -7 and -2 for varied absorption effects. - Remove hardening after positioning; simulate and tweak as needed. - Use fixed needles to assist in positioning. - Draw a rough inner line around embroidery for bead placement with copper wire: - Avoid placing wire too close to edge to prevent OBJ breakage.

simulate and tweak as needed. - Use fixed needles to assist in positioning. - Draw a rough inner line around embroidery for bead placement with copper wire: - Avoid placing wire too close to edge to prevent OBJ breakage. - Delete unnecessary boards after cutting. --- ## Fixing Embroidery with Eye-Catching Points This section discusses stabilizing embroidery positioning using eye-catching points and layer settings. - Add eye-catching points along embroidery edges and some in the middle. - Select all points and set their layer to 2. - Adjust opacity of eye-catching points to 0 to make them invisible. - Delete fixed needles after securing points. - Simulate to confirm stable embroidery position. - Adjust pressure to -1 for slight fabric absorption. --- ## Creating Beaded Embroidery with Threads and Beads This section covers drawing thread lines and applying various bead types for detailed embroidery. - Draw inner thread lines on embroidery using Ctrl + curve sketch; double-click to finish. - Set inner line border width to 2.5 mm with hooked ends. - Extend bead count to 3 or 4 to match beam width (~3 mm). - Use materials: beam slices, round beads, interval beads, tube beads. - Add bead layers with varying colors and transparency for petal shading: - Darker petals with light color overlays. - Light yellow for additional petal layers. - Use free line tool set to white for small pearl effects. - Hook beads along inner lines and smooth corners with editor line tool. - Create lighting effects by drawing multiple inner lines and adding color gradients. - Adjust line thickness and width for realistic highlights. - Use golden tube beads for oatmeal color effect with diameter 0.5 and length 1.5. - Modify bead colors and inner colors for richness. - Add flower petals with buttons and small pearls, adjusting size and materials for shine. - Create pearl leaves with gradients by drawing central and inner lines, deleting excess, and adjusting bead color to match silk or metal materials. --- ## Advanced Skirt Detailing Using New Stitch and Tear Methods This section describes using CLO3D’s new paper editor, stitch tearing, and edge tearing tools to create realistic torn edges and furrowing on skirt layers. - Untwist upper body and simulate front and back pieces separately. - Furrowing with sewing thread tearing requires rum stripping effect. - Add 5 mm internal groove compassion to plate lines. - Use sewing line tearing tool to add tears along sewing lines. - Tear effect created physically via simulation, no need for manual shape creation. - Freeze and pull edges to see natural torn edges. - Save torn edge effects by right-clicking and saving the plate. - Use editor tearing function to adjust line density, thickness, length, and direction for hair-cutting effects.

toggle off to simulate. - New needle methods: - Circle method: creates circular needle structures. - Circle and corner methods for hollow lace effects. - Customize horizontal line number, line thickness, circle density. - Set twist direction (left/right) and upper/lower layer needles for flower patterns. - Create hollow lace using loop density and thread thickness adjustments. - Apply floating threads and enlarge flat data for evenness. - Simulate and apply to visualize lace needle effects. --- ## Final Assembly, Posture Adjustments, and Accessories This section explains posture changes, avoiding cloth penetration, and adding accessories from CLO Connect. - Change model posture with included free material postures. - Reverse-activated virtual model
